text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone who works with it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, descriptive names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another good practice is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and change. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because other developers can quickly find and fix problems. In short, writing readable code today prevents confusion and costly mistakes tomorrow.
